ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Articles L.561-1 et seq., L.562-1 et seq., and R.561-1 et seq.; Code de commerce Book II registration rules for SAS; Ordonnance n° 2016-1635 of 8 December 2016 and Décret n° 2017-1094 of 6 June 2017 transposing and implementing EU AML Directives (AMLD4/AMLD5/AMLD6); Décret n° 2021-300 of 18 March 2021 on the Guichet Unique and INPI formalities; TRACFIN framework and ACPR/AMF joint AML/CFT guidelines.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or sworn legal representative of the ultimate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization where executed outside France

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and original proof of residential address for all directors, signatories, and beneficial owners (UBOs)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with certified French translation for registration

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization if demanded by the receiving French bank; standard banking letter accepted without legalization when issued by an EU/EEA credit institution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, signatories, and authorized users against the TRACFIN domestic intelligence database, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council sanctions (including 1267/1988/2231), and FATF public statements. Risk-based PEP assessment applies to any PEP or family member/close associate holding more than 10% of shares or control. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, unusual wire transfer patterns, and customers displaying inconsistent telematics-dispatch business profiles. Screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years in accordance with French AML/CFT recordkeeping rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises operated by INPI via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; RCS registration maintained by the Greffe du tribunal de commerce
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A SAS corporate name may be expressed in French or in a foreign language provided it uses Latin (Roman) script. Names originating in non-Latin scripts, including Chinese, Arabic, Hebrew, or Cyrillic, must be transliterated into Latin characters for the RCS registration. The name must be linguistically neutral, not misleading, distinct from active RCS entries and prior INPI trademarks, and compliant with the French language policy applicable to mandatory corporate documents under the loi Toubon.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The eight-week name reservation at the relevant Greffe may be renewed once for a further eight-week period when incorporation is pending. If the Guichet Unique notifies a rejection due to conflict with an active RCS name, trademark, or public policy ground, the applicant must file a reasoned recours gracieux with the Greffier en chef within 15 calendar days. If the rejection is maintained, a formal judicial appeal lies before the commercial chamber of the Tribunal judiciaire within two months of notification. Alternatively, the applicant may resubmit the incorporation file with amended secondary names while preserving the existing articles of association, and must retain all rejection notices in the KYC compliance audit trail.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a low-risk, license-free logistics telematics SaaS business. Administrative domiciliation by an approved third-party domiciliation company is lawful under Article L.123-11 of the Code de commerce and is sufficient for RCS and tax registration provided the French address is verifiable and the service agreement is in force. Home domiciliation at the legal representative's residence is also available for a limited renewable period. The registered office must not be a mere mail-drop where tax substance or VAT registration is challenged, therefore all statutory registers, board minutes, and accounting records must be retrievable at the domiciliation address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated annual likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection is approximately 5% for this low-risk, license-free ISIC 6201 SaaS and transportation support activity. Unannounced visits are most plausible during VAT verification, corporate income tax audit, or a company-registry integrity check. All corporate, accounting, and UBO records must be physically or digitally presentable within 48 hours at the registered office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-1 to L.210-6 (general provisions), L.227-1 to L.227-20 (Société par Actions Simplifiée), and R.123-1 et seq. (RCS registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) administered by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; filings processed through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs (Articles of Association) submitted via the Guichet Unique with supporting declarations; registration confirmed by the Extrait Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for an SAS; shareholders freely determine the capital in the Statuts. Capital must be fully subscribed. Monetary contributions must be deposited into a blocked bank account until registration; the Statuts may allow payment of up to 50% on formation, with the remainder due within five years. In-kind contributions exceeding €7,500 in value require a statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Apports) unless an exemption applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The sole shareholder of FR SAS resolves: (1) The subscription and full payment of the issued share capital, as recorded in the Articles of Association, are ratified. (2) The registered office is fixed at 12 Rue de la Paix, 75002 Paris, France. (3) Mr. Jean Dupont is appointed President and legal representative for all purposes, with power to execute any act on behalf of the Company. (4) Mrs. Marie Martin is appointed General Manager, with delegated operational authority. (5) The President is authorized to complete all formalities before the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, publish the mandatory legal notice, and sign all documents relating to incorporation. This resolution takes effect immediately upon signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Verification and Drafting of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel or notary; business name availability verified through the RCS/INPI database.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a French attorney to verify that the proposed corporate name is not already registered and is available on the INPI/RCS search. Draft the Statuts in accordance with the SAS regime, customizing governance provisions, share transfers, and decision-making rules. Execute the Statuts by electronic signature or in writing with all shareholders and the initial President.
required_dossiers: Name availability search result
Passport or national ID of each shareholder
Proof of address of shareholders
Draft Statuts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing prior right, amend the name and re-run the search; the Statuts may also be revised to correct errors and re-executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Bank Account and Deposit of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank selected by the company or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Statuts are signed, open a bank account in the name of the future entity and deposit the amount of subscribed share capital. Obtain the 'attestation de blocage de fonds' evidencing the deposit and the blocked nature of the funds pending registration. Ensure that the bank certificate identifies the company name, account holders, and capital amount.
required_dossiers: Signed Statuts
Shareholder list and subscription commitments
Identification documents of the company representatives
Proof of the intended registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines to open the account, provide supplementary KYC documentation and a business plan; alternatively, use an escrow service or a fintech banking partner, then obtain a new certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Announcement in a Notice Journal (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A legal announcement journal (Journal d'Annonces Légales) authorized by the prefecture in the registered office department.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the 'avis de constitution' containing the company name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate object, and duration of the company. Submit the text to an approved JAL for publication. Obtain an attestation de parution, which is a mandatory component of the incorporation dossier.
required_dossiers: Extract of Statuts with the required legal particulars
Proof of the registered office address
Request for publication signed by the President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the announcement is not legally compliant or contains omissions, publish a corrigendum in the same JAL within 30 days; the attestation de parution is then reissued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the Incorporation Dossier via the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (single online portal operated by INPI), guichet-entreprises.fr.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log onto the Guichet Unique and create the company file. Complete the M0 forms, upload the signed Statuts, the bank capital attestation, the legal advertisement certificate, proof of registered office, and the beneficial owner declaration. Submit the dossier electronically; the portal automatically routes it to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and subsequent authorities.
required_dossiers: Signed Statuts (PDF)
Bank attestation of capital deposit
JAL publication notice
Proof of registered office (lease or domiciliation agreement)
Form M0 and beneficial owner declaration
Identity documents of directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, the portal provides an error report; correct the identified fields and resubmit. In case of repeated refusal, file a direct appeal to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce or seek judicial review before the commercial court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the RCS and Issuance of Extrait Kbis
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within whose territorial jurisdiction the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Guichet Unique validation and payment of the applicable fees, the Greffe enters the company in the RCS. Verify the register entry and obtain the official 'Extrait Kbis', which constitutes the conclusive proof of legal existence and representation. The Kbis is used for all commercial and banking formalities.
required_dossiers: Incorporation application transmitted by the Guichet Unique
Proof of payment of registration fees
Copy of the Kbis request receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis is not issued within the legal time limit, follow up directly with the Greffe and, if necessary, apply for a court order compelling issuance. For substantive errors, request a correction form from the Greffe or lodge a legal nullity claim.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE, Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), and URSSAF, via the Guichet Unique's automatic data transfer.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm automated assignment of the SIREN, SIRET, APE code, and VAT number by INSEE and DGFiP. Register the company for corporate income tax (IFU), VAT, and employer payroll taxes. If cross-border services exceed relevant thresholds, apply for an EORI number for customs purposes. Notify URSSAF of the planned employment arrangements for any staff.
required_dossiers: Extrait Kbis
Statuts
Bank account details (IBAN/BIC)
Tax filing forms (e.g., Form 3160) if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the identifiers are not issued automatically, contact the Guichet Unique helpline or the local DGFiP/URSSAF office to reassign missing codes; rectify data through the portal and obtain updated registrations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 6201 computer programming is not subject to industrial zoning or manufacturing licensing. For any ancillary physical logistics establishment, the Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS) may require a declaration of installation if premises are used for dispatch operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required — the SAS operates as a software and telematics service provider. If the company later installs data centers or a physical warehouse, an 'autorisation d'exploitation' may be necessary under the environmental Code.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) and ADEME (Agence de l'Environnement et de la Maîtrise de l'Énergie)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — software activities do not constitute an ICPE installation or require an environmental impact assessment. Ancillary offices and dispatch facilities may qualify for 'non-classified' status or require simple registration orders under the environmental Code.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the French Environmental Code for waste handling, especially the DEEE/WEEE Directive (2012/19/EU); adherence to EU Regulation 517/2014 on fluorinated greenhouse gases for any HVAC/refrigeration equipment; and compliance with general duty-of-care principles for electronic equipment disposal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the office premises, obtain a fire safety certificate from the municipal Commission de Sécurité before occupation. The building must comply with the Code du travail workplace safety standards and the load-bearing structural requirements of the Code de la Construction et de l'Habitation. No specific occupational license is required for software-development employees, but a health and safety assessment must be documented.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), administered through the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). The principal online portal is impots.gouv.fr. Corporate formation and registration data are submitted through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), with SIREN and SIRET numbers issued through the national business register infrastructure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is incorporated and declared through the INPI Guichet unique. The filing generates the entity's SIREN and SIRET identifiers and communicates formation data to the DGFiP. The SAS must identify its registered tax office, submit its corporate tax and VAT registration information, and activate its professional account on impots.gouv.fr. The French VAT identification number is generally formatted as FR followed by a two-character validation key and the nine-digit SIREN. A non-resident entity without a French fixed establishment must apply to the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE), provide its incorporation certificate, constitutional documents, foreign tax registration evidence, business description, contracts and invoices, identity and authority documents for representatives, and banking and contact details. The entity must distinguish between transactions requiring French VAT registration, transactions subject to customer reverse charge, and transactions reportable through an applicable One Stop Shop regime. EU businesses may generally avoid French VAT registration for B2B services where the customer accounts for VAT under the reverse-charge mechanism, but registration remains necessary for French taxable supplies not covered by reverse charge, domestic imports, local stock, or other French VAT liabilities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, or IS) on its taxable profits. A qualifying SAS may elect temporary taxation under the personal income tax regime (impôt sur le revenu, or IR) for up to five financial years, subject to statutory ownership, activity, size, age and shareholder requirements; the election must be made within the prescribed period and is generally irrevocable once the election period has expired. A qualifying family-owned company may have separate eligibility rules, but those rules do not ordinarily apply to a standard SAS. France has no general United States-style check-the-box election. French anti-hybrid mismatch rules implement the EU ATAD II framework and may deny deductions, impose inclusion, or neutralize imported mismatch outcomes; they do not create a general elective hybrid classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 37,500 annual turnover for the ordinary French VAT franchise threshold applicable to services, including many SaaS and electronically supplied service activities. A tolerance threshold of EUR 41,250 may apply where the preceding-year threshold was not exceeded, subject to current statutory conditions. Separate thresholds apply to goods and certain regulated activities. The threshold does not eliminate VAT obligations for transactions subject to special place-of-supply rules, imports, intra-Community acquisitions, domestic reverse-charge obligations, or elective taxation. A French-established SAS exceeding the applicable threshold, or voluntarily opting for VAT taxation, must register and charge or account for VAT as required.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate a universal real-time VAT invoice-clearance system or mandatory digital stamping regime for ordinary private-sector invoices. Domestic B2B e-invoicing reform is being phased in: all businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; large and medium-sized businesses must issue domestic B2B electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; and small and medium-sized businesses must issue them from 1 September 2027, subject to applicable legislative and regulatory implementation. Electronic invoices must be transmitted through an approved private platform or the public invoicing portal infrastructure designated by law. B2C and cross-border transactions may require electronic transaction reporting (e-reporting) under the phased regime. Public-sector invoices are generally submitted through Chorus Pro. Current invoices must contain mandatory French VAT particulars and be retained in an auditable, authentic and integral form; no general pre-clearance API approval is presently required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from France or another EU Member State to a destination outside the EU may be invoiced without French VAT where the supplier, its customs representative, or the customer completes the export formalities and the supplier retains reliable evidence that the goods left the EU customs territory. The treatment is technically a VAT exemption with the right to deduct rather than a domestic 0% rate. SaaS and other services supplied B2B to a customer established outside France are generally taxed according to the place-of-supply rules and may be outside the scope of French VAT or subject to customer reverse charge, rather than being treated as exported goods at 0%. B2C electronically supplied services may be subject to VAT in the customer's country and may require OSS or local registration. Evidence should include customer status and location, contractual scope, service delivery records, invoices, payment records, IP or access records where relevant, and any required reverse-charge wording.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration and Movement Reference Number (MRN), with electronic confirmation of exit from the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, destination and applicable VAT exemption basis
Transport evidence appropriate to the mode of transport, such as bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note, carrier certificate or freight-forwarder exit evidence
Sales contract, purchase order and packing list where relevant
Proof of delivery or destination outside the EU where customs exit evidence alone is insufficient
For services, customer VAT or business-status evidence, customer establishment and location records, contract, invoice, service logs and proof of payment

Intra-Community supply evidence, where applicable, including the customer's valid EU VAT number, transport evidence and required recapitulative statement; an inward remittance certificate is not a general French VAT export requirement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated within 180 days. Export VAT exemption or deduction may be denied or retrospectively clawed back if the supplier cannot prove export, misstates the customer or destination, issues false documentation, or fails to satisfy invoicing and record-retention requirements. The DGFiP may reassess unpaid VAT, deny related input VAT credits, charge late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month, and impose penalties commonly ranging from 10% for certain filing or payment failures to 40% for deliberate failure and up to 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or concealed activity, subject to statutory facts and procedure. Serious fraud may trigger criminal sanctions. Ordinary VAT reassessment periods generally extend through the end of the third year following the year in which the tax became payable, with longer periods available in specified fraudulent, concealed or criminal circumstances. Export evidence, customs data, contracts, invoices and accounting records must be retained for the applicable French statutory period, commonly at least ten years for business accounting records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting with the Eurosystem and the European Central Bank, is the central bank; foreign-exchange administration and balance-of-payments reporting functions are exercised through the French Ministry of Economy and Finance, specifically the Direction Generale du Tresor. Prudential and AML/CFT supervision of credit institutions is conducted by the ACPR (Autorite de Controle Prudentiel et de Resolution) within the Banque de France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both the current account and the capital account. France maintains no exchange-control licensing or prior-authorisation regime for ordinary treasury operations; Article L. 151-1 et seq. of the Code monetaire et financier confirms the free movement of capital. The practical constraints are documentary and statistical: cross-border financial transactions involving non-EEA counterparties are subject to Banque de France balance-of-payments declarations through the servicing bank, and cash or asset movements of EUR 10,000 or more must be reported. Profit remittance hurdles relate to corporate law and tax rather than convertibility: dividends must be paid from distributable reserves under Articles L. 232-11 and L. 232-11-1 of the Code de commerce; the statutory 25% withholding tax under Article 119-2 CGI may be reduced to 0% for qualifying EU/EEA parent companies meeting the 10% holding and two-year condition, or under an applicable double-tax treaty; and payments to residents of non-cooperative states under Article 238-A CGI face enhanced due diligence, non-deductibility, and high withholding rates. A French SAS with non-resident shareholders must therefore prepare a distribution-capacity certificate, a tax-residency certificate for the beneficial owner, and treaty-reduction evidence before any upstream dividend remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France, as a Eurosystem member state, imposes no mandatory surrender, no conversion ratio, and no repatriation window for export proceeds. SaaS and logistics-telematics service exports are classified as invisible current-account transactions and may be invoiced and retained in EUR, USD, or any freely convertible currency without prior approval. The relevant obligation is statistical only: non-EEA payments exceeding EUR 10,000 must be captured in the bank's monthly balance-of-payments declaration to the Banque de France, and the SAS must retain the underlying commercial evidence (signed platform agreement, invoices, payment settlement records, and usage logs) for at least five years for inspection by the ACPR, the Direction Generale des Finances Publiques, and customs authorities. No currency surrender certificate or central-bank approval is needed for the collection of subscription fees from foreign fleet customers.

Capital Deposit Account / Operational Account with SEPA and SWIFT MT103 clearing

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR Account; capital escrow possible via notarial route

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-High for operational disbursement rails and receivables collection; Low for capital escrow and commercial LC issuance. EEA-licensed electronic money institutions such as Qonto, Shine, and Treezor, which are ACPR-supervised, can onboard the SAS remotely and provide EUR IBANs, SEPA Instant Credit Transfers, virtual cards, and some SWIFT outbound coverage. They are not credit institutions and therefore cannot provide the deposit-guarantee status, the capital-subscription attestation, or the commercial letter-of-credit facilities expected by a Bank of France branch and foreign investors. An offshore digital EMI that is not established and authorised in the EEA cannot lawfully hold the company's treasury as a French payment account and is highly likely to be rejected by the statutory auditor and the RCS. Stripe Billing, while compatible with the target payment rails, should be used strictly as a merchant collection gateway with automatic daily sweeps to an ACPR-licensed bank; material liquidity must not be parked with a non-credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML law in Article L. 561-5 and R. 561-5 of the Code monetaire et financier requires the bank to identify the legal entity and its beneficial owners before opening an account, but it does not impose an absolute face-to-face meeting. Remote onboarding is legally available where the bank relies on an ANSSI-qualified or eIDAS-compliant electronic identification and video-verification procedure. In practice, BNP Paribas and Societe Generale will accept a fully remote KYC process for an EEA-resident director but may require one physical appearance at a French branch, or a signature before a French consulate, when the legal representative or the ultimate beneficial owner is resident outside the EEA. The director should be prepared to present the original passport, the Kbis, the certificate of registration of beneficial owners, the SAS by-laws, proof of registered office, and, if relying on remote identification, a notarised and apostilled identity package. A digital-first bank may open the account online, but the more foreign-ownership complexity the onboarding ticket carries, the higher the probability that a physical interview will be requested by the compliance committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner is a non-EEA resident individual with no French connection and the SAS has no local employees, creating a shell-company typology.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled passports of the directors and UBO; original Kbis and RCS registration; extract of the Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs filed with the greffe; notarised ownership chart showing the chain from the SAS to the UBO; audited or management accounts of the ultimate parent; French registered-office lease or co-working agreement; evidence of actual local substance, including the software platform's hosting contract, client contracts, and the director's travel and board-meeting minutes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection originates from a third-party payer or from a personal account of a shareholder rather than from the corporate bank account identified in the corporate register.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement and resolutions of the shareholders; a certified copy of the corporate account statement of the subscribing shareholder; a signed source-of-funds declaration ('declaration d'origine des fonds') for each injection; evidence of the corporate governance chain; confirmation that the remittance name matches the shareholder name in the Register of Beneficial Owners; bank reference letters from the originating bank; and, if available, the deposit certificate issued by the receiving French bank or notary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High recurring cross-border subscription volumes with limited employee headcount, raising suspicions of pass-through invoicing or unlicensed money service activity in the telematics and logistics sector.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed SaaS agreements, order forms, and online acceptance records; detailed platform usage logs showing dispatching, route optimisation, and telematics sessions; cloud and hosting provider invoices matching the revenue volumes; payroll register and employment contracts; organisational chart; customer KYC records for large fleet customers; and an external accountant's confirmation that the company's revenues are reported as operating income and subject to French corporate income tax.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to counterparties established in countries appearing on France's list of non-cooperative states, on the EU list of non-cooperative jurisdictions, or subject to sanctions, particularly when software resellers are involved.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of the counterparty's economic substance: local business licence, premises lease, payroll, and tax registration; registered office certificate and UBO extract; executed distribution or reseller contracts; sanctions and adverse-media screening results against all parties, including the UBOs; negative results from EU, UN, French Treasury, and OFAC screening lists; and a written compliance opinion from the French bank's legal or AML department before the first payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fiscal inconsistency where the directors or tax advisers treat the French SAS as tax-transparent outside France, or where the effective place of management is contested.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French tax-residence certificate issued by the Direction Generale des Finances Publiques; corporate income tax filings for the current and prior period; board minutes and decisions taken in France; French bank account and cash-management records; registered French office lease; and a concise memorandum from the French tax counsel confirming that the SAS has its effective seat of management in France and is subject to Article 209 CGI corporate income tax.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for capital subscriptions requires a French blocked account at an ACPR-licensed bank or a notary-led deposit arrangement. The shareholder sends EUR via SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA transfers or SEPA Credit Transfer for EEA transfers to the blocked account, with the ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' and clear remittance text such as 'CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION - SAS [name] - [RCS pending] - UBO [name]'. The receiving bank verifies the ordering party, the source of funds, sanctions lists, and beneficial ownership; where the deposit is made before RCS registration, the bank or notary issues the deposit certificate required for the company formation file. After the Kbis is issued, the escrowed funds are released to the operational account. For shareholder current-account advances, the purpose code 'LOAN' or the French commercial label 'apport en compte courant d'associe' must be used; the loan agreement must respect the Article 39-6 CGI interest-rate cap on shareholder advances, must be at arm's length, and must not exceed the debtor's distributable-safety thresholds if repaid. All non-EEA inbound receipts equal to or exceeding EUR 10,000 are automatically reported to the Banque de France through the bank's balance-of-payments declaration; no exchange-control approval is required, but the company must retain the share-subscription bank statements, SWIFT UETR, corporate resolutions, and source-of-funds files for five years.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EEA and French disbursements, the primary rail is SEPA Credit Transfer under ISO 20022 pain.001, which covers payroll, hosting fees, telematics data licences, subcontractor fees, and subscription refunds. For non-EEA beneficiaries, the standard rail is SWIFT MT103 carrying a UETR, with exact beneficiary name, IBAN or account number, and a precise purpose text such as 'ROYALTY - TELEMATICS SOFTWARE' or 'CLOUD HOSTING FEES'. Where the SAS procures physical fleet-hardware components from non-EU suppliers in large amounts, an irrevocable documentary letter of credit under UCP 600 issued by BNP, Societe Generale, or CIC and confirmed by the seller's bank is the legally appropriate clearing instrument; at-sight LCs are preferred for high-volume telematics device purchases. Before any outbound transfer to non-cooperative jurisdictions, the company must run restrictive-measures screening against EU, UN, and French Treasury lists and assess Article 238-A CGI non-deductibility and withholding consequences. Any outbound non-EEA transfer of EUR 10,000 or more flows into the Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical report and must be supported by contract, commercial invoice, and receipt of service evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX spot contracts and outright forwards in EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CHF executed with ACPR-licensed credit institutions under an ISDA or French master agreement, used solely to hedge forecast commercial cash flows.
Vanilla European-style FX options in EUR/USD for protection against adverse movements in USD-denominated subscription revenue and vendor payments, with no speculative leverage.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps between EUR and USD, subject to EMIR clearing and margining thresholds, portfolio reconciliation, and reporting to an EU-registered trade repository, with documented hedge effectiveness.

Non-deliverable forwards in restricted-delivery currencies such as CNY or INR with a permitted credit-institution counterparty, where the SAS can evidence actual commercial exposure in those currencies and where the instrument is not entered for speculative or excessive leverage purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts filing (liasseur de comptes annuels) with the commercial registry, including balance sheet, profit-and-loss statement, and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via GUICHET UNIQUE / INPI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year SAS, by 31 July, unless a commercial court extension is granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposition triggers individual director fines up to EUR 10,000 plus administrative strike-off proceedings initiated by the Commercial Court; repeat failure may lead to judicial dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 2065 series) and corporate income tax balance payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal year ending 31 December, due by 3 May; for other year-ends, within 3 months of fiscal close; balance payment due at the same filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing results in a 10% automatic surcharge on unpaid tax, then 0.8% monthly interest; minimum penalty of EUR 1,800 under Article 1728 CGI; deliberate concealment attracts 40%-80% penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholder written resolution (Approval of annual accounts and profit appropriation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book; retained at the registered office for inspection by tax authorities or a statutory auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the fiscal year-end, unless extended by court order; SAS articles may permit written consultation or a unanimous act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain shareholder approval exposes directors to liability for unlawful profit distribution and invalidates the appropriation decision; shareholders may seek dissolution for infra-annual governance failure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner register update and RCS declaration (event-driven annual update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual anniversary date; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days of the change. In addition, assurance of continued accuracy is expected as part of the annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A fine up to EUR 30,000 and two years' imprisonment may apply for intentional failure to disclose UBO changes; late filings also attract registry penalties of up to EUR 5,000

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under French Commercial Code Art. L821-3 (PACTE), a SAS must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) if it exceeds at least two of the three criteria: wholesale balance sheet total exceeding EUR 4,000,000; net turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000; average workforce exceeding 50 employees. A company above the thresholds may obtain exemption if part of a group with a selected consolidated auditor, but the individual SAS remains subject to the criteria unless a group exemption is expressly granted under the law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual and non-consolidated statutory accounts are prepared under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général – Réglementation ANC); consolidated accounts of EU-listed groups adopt IFRS as endorsed by the EU. Mandatory disclosure of sustainability information in the annual report is required under the CSRD when applicable to the entity.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a standalone annual beneficial owner confirmation filing. The SAS must maintain a complete and up-to-date register of beneficial owners (RBO) under Articles L561-46 et seq. of the Monetary and Financial Code. Any share transfer or other act triggering a change in beneficial ownership requires an RCS update within 30 days via the GUICHET UNIQUE. During the annual accounts filing, the registry does not separately require a renewed UBO attestation, but the company's accuracy may be verified through tax and registry controls.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des Mouvements de Titres)
Register of Directors (Register of Shareholder Decisions)
Minute Book (Registre des Décisions et Procès-Verbaux)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$ 250 – 900 (annual fee for SAS business address, corporate suite, or registered agent in major cities excluding accommodation)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$ 6,000 – 20,000 (initial audit of an operating logistics SaaS SAS; subsequent audits typically lower if no group consolidation)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on first €42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs with turnover ≤ €10 million; research tax credit (CIR) up to 30% of eligible R&D expenses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (and annexes 2051-A to 2058-G) filed electronically via EFI (Échange de Formulaires Informatifs) on impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months of fiscal year-end; for calendar year-end (31 Dec), deadline is 3 May (or 15 May if e-filed).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report French-source income only; apply treaty provisions if applicable.
Only losses from French permanent establishment or French-source activities are eligible.
Eligible only if turnover ≤ €10 million and entity is a small or medium enterprise.
Claim only for R&D activities performed in France; substantiate with technical and accounting documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% of tax due, plus 0.5% per month of delay; additional 10% for failure to file after formal notice; interest at 0.20% per month.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% (flat tax) for non-residents, subject to treaty reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Form 5000 (residence certificate) to the French tax authority to claim treaty rate; apply for reduced withholding at source or refund via Form 5001/5002.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory 30% for royalties and interest; treaty rates typically 0-15% depending on jurisdiction and type of income.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €400,000,000 (turnover or assets) for full Master File and Local File; simplified documentation for companies with turnover > €50 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies anti-abuse rules and substance-over-form; no specific ESR, but requires real economic activity for tax residency and treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income, overstatement of deductions, or concealment of taxable transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of 50% of understated tax (for gross negligence) or 80% for abuse of law; criminal penalties up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if they committed fraud or serious misconduct; travel bans and imprisonment possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a French entity without real economic substance, solely to obtain tax benefits or treaty access.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, penalty of 80% for abuse of law, and potential criminal charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held jointly liable for taxes and penalties; may face travel restrictions and criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML procedures, suspicious transaction reporting, or beneficial ownership disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €5 million or 5% of turnover; criminal penalties for money laundering up to 5 years imprisonment and €375,000 fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined and imprisoned; may be banned from managing companies.
